image_prompt.text: A chain of ice platforms spiralling up the mountain, spaced within jumping range so base to peak reads as one ordered climbing route
Lower, middle and upper bands of climbing platforms, each a raised foothold standing clear of the lava floor
Thin ice bridges, frozen trusses and cliff-wall scrambles linking one spiral section to the next
The floor is lava — the ground far below the mountain is lethal on contact, so a missed jump off any platform kills
A large snowy base platform at the foot of the mountain where several players gather before setting off up the climb
A wide safe platform at the very summit, flat and open enough for a group of players to stand on
The ice mountain itself — sheer frozen cliff walls rising about 100 studs from the wide snowy base to the peak, in icy blue and white
Ice crystal formations growing out of the platforms and cliff faces, cyan and glowing with neon accents

layout_placement.text: The end-of-course reward point on the summit platform, triggered when a climber reaches the top

notes: Close dominance call: the prompt self-declares a "floor is lava" survival game, but everything described is a vertical jump-from-platform-to-platform climb, so Obby & Platformer leads and owns the shape and the genre-wide P6. Survival is named second and contributes hazard-kill (the lava floor as the thing being survived) and terrain-tiered (raised safe ground above it); its shape was not taken.

Preset Tower Obby taken with its shape and three of its four options; obstacle-timing (platforms that vanish after being stepped on) was dropped because the prompt describes a fixed structure of climbable parts.

Shape course-tower carries P2 because a spiral ascent puts platforms directly above each other. P2 is not ready yet; the fallback that stays on the proven pipeline is course-terraced (P6 + tiered), an ascending hillside climb with nothing overhanging. Deferred, not silently downgraded.
terrain-relief and terrain-tiered each carry P0 + tiered, which is subsumed by the shape's P2 and so is not listed separately in pipeline.

Stated dimensions carried in text rather than count: about 100 studs high, and wide enough for multiple players. No count field applies — no quantity of objects was given ("multiple levels", lower/middle/upper).
Palette for the image model: icy blue, white and cyan with some neon accents, folded into the option texts.

would have asked: Sounds like a tower climb — a spiral course of ice platforms wrapping up the mountain from a wide snowy base, thin ice bridges and cliff scrambles between sections, a wide safe platform at the summit, and the lava floor lethal below. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: the spiral means platforms sit directly above each other, which needs the overhanging-surfaces route and that one isn't ready yet — is a stepped hillside ascent with nothing overhanging acceptable instead, or should I hold for the overhang build?
would have asked: the tower preset normally includes thin ice that cracks and drops away a moment after you step on it — should the thin ice bridges be breakable, or stay solid?
